run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The social-network front door is broken: the openresty-based nginx-thrift pod (nginx-thrift-65f656c999-mchfs) is not ready, its container was OOMKilled (exit 137) and is in CrashLoopBackOff with 3 restarts while the other 26 pods in the namespace are Ready with 0 restarts. The nginx-thrift Service therefore has no ready address, its blackbox probe_success stayed 0 through the last sampled point inside the window (23:02:45Z) while sibling services returned to 1, and the wrk2 load test against /wrk2-api/post/compose reported 264 requests in 10.01s with 'Socket errors: write 3468, timeout 9'. The only configuration difference I found is that the nginx-thrift Deployment pod template carries a 256Mi memory limit / 128Mi request while every other Deployment in the namespace has no resources set at all; two ReplicaSets of the same image prove the limit was added by a 'kubectl-patch' Update at 23:02:31Z, which is the only non-Helm change to any of the 27 Deployments. A full end-to-end trace at 23:02:54Z shows the whole downstream chain (compose-post, text, user-mention, url-shorten, media, unique-id, user, post-storage, user-timeline, home-timeline, social-graph) answering in single-digit milliseconds with HTTP 200, so the downstream services were healthy and are not the cause. The memory limit is the leading root cause: it is the sole workload-level setting introduced during the window and it is on the workload that is OOMKilling. The conclusion is partial because the OOMKilled terminations themselves were only visible in object state read after the authorized window ended (query observed_at ~23:04Z), so I could not time the OOMs or watch the container approach 256Mi inside the window, and the change-history integration is not available to confirm who issued the patch.

claims.text: At 23:04:01Z the pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-mchfs had container nginx-thrift not ready, restartCount 2, waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff, and lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 (startedAt 23:03:21Z, finishedAt 23:03:33Z).

At 23:04:41Z, nginx-thrift-65f656c999-mchfs was the only unhealthy pod in namespace social-network: Ready=False, container nginx-thrift restartCount 3, lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled, state.waiting.reason CrashLoopBackOff; all other 26 pods were Ready=True with restartCount 0.

Deployment nginx-thrift has a container memory limit of 256Mi and memory request of 128Mi; of the 27 Deployments in social-network it is the only one with any resources.limits or resources.requests set at all.

The limit was added after the Helm install: ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df was created 23:02:17Z with resources {} , while ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 was created 23:02:31Z with limits memory 256Mi and requests memory 128Mi; the two pod templates are otherwise identical (same image ghcr.io/sregym/openresty-thrift:20261109-trace-identity, same env fqdn_suffix, same init container alpine-container, same volumes/mounts).

Deployment nginx-thrift's managedFieldsSummary shows helm Apply at 23:02:15Z followed by a kubectl-patch Update at 23:02:31Z (generation 2); every other Deployment in social-network is still generation 1 with only helm Apply and kube-controller-manager status Updates, so nginx-thrift is the only workload patched after install.

Inside the window the nginx-thrift ReplicaSet rollout is visible: nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df was scaled up at 23:02:17Z, nginx-thrift-65f656c999 scaled up at 23:02:31Z, pod nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-6rszd stopped at 23:02:35Z, pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-vctbc stopped at 23:02:45Z and pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-mchfs created at 23:02:45Z; the events also record a FailedMount for volume nginx-thrift-config on nginx-thrift-65f656c999-vctbc at 23:02:32Z.

At 23:04:59Z the Service endpoints for nginx-thrift in social-network contained only notReadyAddresses (pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-mchfs, 10.244.234.149) on port 8080, i.e. no ready backend, and no NetworkPolicy exists in the social-network namespace that could block traffic.

Deployment nginx-thrift reported status condition Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable ('Deployment does not have minimum availability', lastUpdateTime 23:03:34Z) and unavailableReplicas 1, while observedGeneration 2 and updatedReplicas 1.

blackbox probe_success for instance nginx-thrift.social-network:8080 (job blackbox-social-network) was 0 at every sampled point from 23:00:45Z through 23:02:45Z, while several sibling instances in the same job (e.g. home-timeline-service.social-network:9090, media-service.social-network:9090, url-shorten-service.social-network:9090, compose-post-service.social-network:9090, unique-id-service.social-network:9090) changed from 0 to 1 in the same samples.

The wrk2 load generator (pod wrk2-job-86rgq, namespace social-network) logged for its round against http://10.96.159.248:8080/wrk2-api/post/compose: '264 requests in 10.01s', 'Requests/sec: 26.38', 'Socket errors: connect 0, read 0, write 3468, timeout 9', plus many 'reconnect_socket' lines; the log lines were written 23:02:45Z-23:02:53Z.

The openresty nginx-thrift container logged repeated worker crashes: '[alert] 1#1: worker process 15/20/21 exited on signal 11' from pod nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-6rszd at 23:02:35Z and worker processes 16/17/25 exited on signal 11 from pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-vctbc at 23:02:45Z.

Downstream dependencies were working during the window: a complete trace at 23:02:54Z (trace_id 020bc9d4039649e5) shows nginx-web-server POST /wrk2-api/post/compose returning http.status_code 200 in 7.7ms with the whole chain healthy - compose-post-service compose_post_server 6.7ms, media-service compose_media_server 11us, unique-id-service 21us, text-service compose_text_server 1.7ms, user-service compose_creator_server 15us, user-mention-service 1.1ms, url-shorten-service 975us, post-storage-service store_post_server 724us, user-timeline-service 1.2ms, home-timeline-service 1.37ms, social-graph-service get_followers_server 1.08ms - with zero error_rows in every span group.

The only application error lines logged anywhere in social-network during 22:30:00Z-23:02:55Z were transient mongodb 'Failed to create mongodb index ... serverSelectionTimeoutMS expired' retries at 23:02:16Z-23:02:20Z while the mongo pods were still starting (user-service, post-storage-service, url-shorten-service, user-timeline-service); no runtime error lines from any service other than those startup retries and the wrk2 socket errors were returned.

The Jaeger tracing reporter configuration is identical for all services in the namespace (otel-collector.observe.svc.cluster.local:6831, queueSize 1000000, bufferFlushInterval 10, sampler probabilistic 0.01), and the otel-collector Service exists in namespace observe on port 6831, so no service-specific tracing configuration distinguishes nginx-thrift.

Prometheus rules show the nginx-thrift symptoms pending at 23:03:49Z-23:04:09Z: ServiceEndpointDown 'Service endpoint nginx-thrift.social-network:8080 in social-network is unreachable' (probe_success == 0), PodStatusError with reason CrashLoopBackOff on pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-mchfs, and KubePodNotReady for the same pod; the HighRequestErrorRate/HighRequestLatency rules based on traces_span_metrics_calls_total were inactive.

The nginx-thrift container's working set was only 2.72 MB at the last in-window sample (23:02:55Z), i.e. well below the 256Mi limit before traffic-induced growth; container_spec_memory_limit_bytes returned no series for this pod, so the cgroup limit value itself was not readable from cadvisor.

Root cause: the 256Mi memory limit added to the nginx-thrift container by the kubectl-patch on Deployment nginx-thrift at 23:02:31Z is too small for openresty under the wrk2 load; the container exceeds it, is OOMKilled (exit 137), enters CrashLoopBackOff, and the nginx-thrift Service is left with no ready endpoint, which is what fails the front-door requests and the blackbox probe.

Secondary contributor: the 23:02:31Z patch also forced a rolling replacement of the namespace's single nginx-thrift replica (pods stopped at 23:02:35Z and 23:02:45Z), so part of the writetime/timeout socket errors seen by wrk2 between 23:02:42Z and 23:02:52Z is connection loss during that rollout; this alone would be transient and does not explain the pod remaining unavailable afterwards.

Rejected: a failing downstream social-network microservice. The full 33-span trace at 23:02:54Z shows every downstream hop (compose-post, text, user-mention, url-shorten, media, unique-id, user, post-storage, user-timeline, home-timeline, social-graph) succeeding in about 1-7ms with HTTP 200 and no error spans, all 26 other pods are Ready with 0 restarts, and their logs contain only startup mongodb index retries.

Rejected: a NetworkPolicy or Service/Endpoints misconfiguration blocking the front door. There are no NetworkPolicy objects in social-network, and the nginx-thrift Service/Endpoints object exists and points at the single pod, listing it under notReadyAddresses rather than being absent.

Increase or remove the 256Mi memory limit on Deployment nginx-thrift (for example restore the limit-free template used by ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df, or raise it well above observed usage) and re-check container_memory_working_set_bytes against the limit while the wrk2 load runs.

gaps: The OOMKilled terminations of nginx-thrift-65f656c999-mchfs (startedAt 23:03:21Z, finishedAt 23:03:33Z) and the CrashLoopBackOff status were read from live object state at observed_at 23:04:01Z and 23:04:41Z, i.e. after the authorized window ended at 23:02:55Z; the exact OOM timestamps and restart count inside the window are unknown.

No in-window metric shows the nginx-thrift container approaching its 256Mi limit: the only cadvisor sample available for the current pod inside the window is 2719744 bytes at 23:02:55Z, and container_spec_memory_limit_bytes returned no series for this pod.

The change-history integration is not available, so I cannot confirm which operator or tool issued the kubectl-patch on Deployment nginx-thrift at 23:02:31Z or what its declared intent was; the patch attribution comes only from managedFieldsSummary (last write per manager).

Prometheus in this target carries no traces_span_metrics_calls_total / rpc_* application series (get_label_values on traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned no data), so per-service error-rate and latency alert evaluation inside the window could not be checked; the trace evidence is a biased Jaeger sample, not a failure rate.

Application logs after 23:02:55Z were not readable within the authorized window, so the current pod's own log lines (including any further 'worker process exited on signal 11' messages) are unknown, and the single-sample segfault lines seen on the two earlier pods were logged in the same second those pods were stopped, so they cannot be separated from shutdown behaviour.

Pod wrk2-job-86rgq produced more log lines than could be read (200 of 200 rows returned, 140 omitted in the read slice); its rounds after 23:02:53Z and the final error totals of the load test are unknown.
next_steps: Confirm the intent and author of the kubectl-patch Update on Deployment nginx-thrift at 2026-11-23T23:02:31Z (the change that added limits.memory=256Mi / requests.memory=128Mi) using cluster audit logs or change history.

Once the limit is raised or removed, re-run the wrk2 /wrk2-api/post/compose load and capture container_memory_working_set_bytes for the nginx-thrift container against the cgroup limit to confirm the memory-exhaustion mechanism.
Collect the nginx-thrift container log and kubelet OOM/eviction events for the period after 23:02:55Z to time the OOM kills that this investigation could only observe as terminal state.
